To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the centromere of fission yeast has a unique chromatin organization that is essential for proper DNA replication.

(i) Swi6 is not required for early centromere replication, but rather for early centromeric replication, (ii) Chp1 is also required for centromeric replication timing and (iii) histone methylation is required to maintain the early centromeric origin of DNA replication.

(1) the centromere is an active site for transcription and RNA processing during replication, (2) the centromeric chromatin state is maintained during replication by the RNAi machinery, and (3) histone methylation is not required for early replication of the centromere.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of histone methylation on gene expression.
the regulation of the cell division cycle, and the molecular basis of the control of gene expression.
the mechanisms of centromeric heterochromatin maintenance and the role of heterochromatin for replication timing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
histone modifications, RNAi and RNA polymerase II are all required for early replication of the centromere.
the replication timing of pericentromeric regions is regulated by a complex interplay between histone modifications and the transcriptional machinery.

the replication timing in centromere region is affected by the RNAi machinery and the RNAi machinery is affected by histone methylation, however replication is not directly affected by the RNA polymerase II.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the histone H3 lysine 9 methylation is required for early replication of the fission yeast centromere.
the centromere replication timing is determined by the interplay between RNAi and histone methylation.

histone methylation and RNAi are important to maintain the heterochromatin structure in centromere and that disruption of histone methylation can lead to early replication timing, but that RNAi is also important to ensure the proper replication timing in the centromeric region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the centromere is a unique chromatin structure that has a specific role in the control of DNA replication.
the timing of DNA replication is a complex and highly regulated process.
replication timing is a dynamic process in which different mechanisms are at work in centromeres and in euchromatin, and that histone methylation is only one of these mechanisms.
